body: The calendar retains displayed event inputs after an identical ordinary read. Changed versions, projection fields, editability, order and membership still publish; no source-response cache or reduced page bounds are introduced. With 1,000 cards and 995 dated items, seven-sample no-change refresh medians improve from 155 to 37 ms locally and from 879 to 352 ms under network/CPU emulation. Every sample still makes one Calendar read and retains all items. The combined full gate passes 251 Rust, 137 JavaScript and 12 Python tests; broad HTTPS/planning, seven Chromium and six WebKit suites pass, including real source updates and the failing unoptimized control. The existing manual app is rebuilt/restarted: all 34 prior resource versions, pins, preferences and certificate are preserved, and all 33 HTTPS assets are verified. Evidence: progress/2026-09-30-calendar-refresh.md. Initial/changed-page rendering, physical-device acceptance and the durable-write target remain open. Scope and card acceptance are unchanged.

metadata.summary: Unchanged calendar refresh is faster and verified
